One familiar series idea applied once; heavy L'Hospital is optional.

questions.justification: Two small topics chained: grouped-data mean deviation then binomial tail; options available.

questions.justification: Single standard image-of-a-point formula (or 30/60 degree geometry).

questions.justification: One standard 1^infinity trick plus a short expansion.

questions.key_step: Equate values and derivatives at x=1
questions.justification: Two equations; no decision involved.

questions.justification: One recognised substitution, then a standard integral.

questions.key_step: Second derivative test
questions.justification: Direct evaluation, no decision.

questions.justification: One idea with two cases and a boundary-inclusion check; options help.

questions.justification: Short and direct once the right angle is seen.

questions.key_step: Count 2 men and 2 women
questions.justification: Single counting formula.

questions.justification: Conditional probability with one binomial computation; familiar.

questions.justification: One familiar move.

questions.justification: One familiar move (one-sided limits with GIF/fractional part) with a small trap on the left side.

questions.justification: Standard trigonometric substitution twice.

questions.justification: One familiar condition; two short equations.

questions.key_step: f(c)=0 implies g(c)<0, so roots are distinct
questions.justification: The distinct-roots argument is a non-obvious step and there are no options to check against (numerical answer); IVT used twice; one level above 2021-P2-Q3 (L2) because the answer is numerical.

questions.key_step: Transform A and B (or the line) and test opposite sides
questions.justification: Axes shifted and rotated, then a sign test; precision risk in transformation signs with no options.

questions.key_step: Image of the intersection point and of one more point
questions.justification: Routine reflection chain with a numerical answer.

questions.key_step: Homogenise with (x+y)/k = 1 and set a+b = 0
questions.justification: Standard homogenisation then a quadratic; two chapters combined.

questions.key_step: Equal priors: posterior proportional to C(w,2)
questions.justification: Bayes with three urns, routine chain, numerical; easier than 2025-P2-Q11 (L3) because the urns have equal sizes and equal priors.
